title: Syracuse - Defund Palantir
description:
Join us as we demand to Defund Palantir, a private corporation, started by Peter Thiel on August 23!

Why?

By 2010, Palantir had become a favorite among U.S. government agencies involved in counterterrorism and fraud detection. They expanded into commercial markets in the mid-2010s, offering big data tools for finance, healthcare, and manufacturing.

Controversial contracts with Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) drew scrutiny starting in 2017, especially regarding deportation tracking systems.

Most recently the Army bundled $10 billion in contracts with them for 10 years and now Peter Thiel has decided to get back involved in politics.

As a private corporation, billions of our tax payer dollars are going to fund:

-Surveillance & Civil Liberties Violations - Including ICE

-Militarization of Artificial Intelligence

-Collaboration with Foreign Governments - Including Israeli targeting of civilians

-Corporate Secrecy & Lack of Accountability

-Government Influence & No-Bid Contracts

-Use in Public Health Without Consent

-Policing & Predictive Analytics

-Worker Surveillance & Anti-Labor Use

Note: We beleive in non-violence. This is a peaceful protest.

title: WORKERS OVER BILLIONAIRES - Labor Day (May Day/50501) National Day of Protest
description:
Join Ohio District 14 Partners, District 14 Voice, Progress NEO, Foods Not Bombs, Like-Minded Lake County, Good Trouble Trumbull, and Burning Bridge Brigade on Labor Day to let this administration know we are nearing the end before more drastic, economic actions are taken. We will begin our protest by hearing from some of our legislators as to where we go from here. We will hear encouraging words from former Representative John Patterson at 11:00 a.m. at the Bainbridge City Hall before moving along 306 with our signs and enthusiasm.

The billionaires continue to wage a cruel war on working people, with their cronies in the administration, ICE and law enforcement backing up their attacks. This Labor Day we will continue to stand strong, fighting for public schools over private profits, healthcare over hedge funds, shared prosperity over corporate politics.

Working people built this nation and we know how to take care of each other. We won’t back down—we will never stop fighting for our families and the rights and freedoms that ensure access to opportunity and a better life for all Americans. The billionaire's time is up.

On September 1st we will continue the movement we launched together on May 1st, No Kings Day, standing in solidarity with all our communities under attack and fighting for real wins for all our people.

In thousands of communities around the country we encourage you to take a stand with us on Labor Day. On the streets, outside the offices of the corporate criminals who are behind the attacks on our freedoms and at congressional offices. Together we will demand a world that works for all of us.

OUR DEMANDS TO BUILD THE SOCIETY WE ALL DESERVE:

Stop the billionaire takeover and rampant corruption of the Trump administration.

Protect and defend Medicaid, Social Security, and other programs for working people.

Fully funded schools, and healthcare and housing for all.

Stop the attacks on immigrants, Black, indigenous, trans people, and all our communities.

Invest in people not wars.

Please note: A core principle behind all our events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values. Weapons of any kind, including those legally permitted, should not be brought to events.

title: Climate Superfund Strike: Make Polluters Pay!
description:
On August 14 at 11 AM, we’re mobilizing in front of the Hoboken Pier A  — a site that flooded during Hurricane Sandy — to demand bold action: it’s time for New Jersey to pass the Climate Superfund Act and Make Polluters Pay.

Youth leaders from across the state are coming together to make our voices heard. Joined by mayors from across the region, legislative champions of the bill, and key statewide representatives, this is our moment to show exactly where New Jersey’s future stands.

This action is about more than just one bill — it’s about climate justice, accountability, and refusing to let another legislative session go by without real solutions that put affordability for average New Jerseyans first. With the Legislature set to return this fall, we’re using this August moment to send a clear message: we expect movement, not delay, post the Climate Superfund Act.

title: Air Permitting in Wisconsin & How It Impacts Our Health
description:
Wisconsin's utility regulatory system is failing the public with permitting processes that support industry, not the people. The agencies responsible for making these decisions cannot deny a permit based on health or environmental impact if technical requirements are met, regardless of real-world harm.

Join us on Wednesday, August 20th at 4:30pm to learn more about the WI Department of Natural Resources' role in the utility regulatory system, potential flaws in their air permitting process and how it affects the health and wellbeing of Wisconsinites, and what steps can be taken to advocate for ourselves and our communities.

Speakers include: Dr. Brittany Keyes, Healthy Climate Wisconsin; Jayne Black, Moms Clean Air Force, and Kat Klawes, Citizen Action of Wisconsin. There will be time for Q&A at the end of the presentation.

title: Tell Camden City Council: Hold EMR Accountable!
description:
The City of Camden has released a $6.7 million agreement with EMR—one of the largest metal recycling companies in the world—following the massive February fire that sent toxic smoke through Waterfront South and beyond.

**But here’s the problem:
Most of that money is going right back into EMR’s own facilities, and the company itself controls half the seats on the funding committee, including the Chair. Waterfront South residents—those most impacted—have zero elected representation on how these funds will be used.**

**We’re inviting all Camden, South Jersey, and Philly neighbors, organizers, and allies to join us in speaking at the next Camden City Council meeting to demand:**

*Independent, community-led oversight of the EMR fund*

*Real investment in health and safety for residents*

*Transparency and public accountability from the City and EMR*

📅Tuesday
🕔 5PM–7PM
📍 Camden City Hall | 520 Market Street, Camden, NJ

This is a peaceful effort to reclaim community power and make sure those most impacted have a real seat at the table.

Let’s show up for Camden—and for environmental justice.

title: Granville Fall Canvass Kickoff – Municipal Elections
description:
Join us as we launch our Fall Canvass for the Granville County municipal elections! Canvassing is the most effective way to reach voters face-to-face, build relationships in our community, and make sure every voice is heard on Election Day. Whether you’ve never knocked on a door before or you’re a seasoned volunteer, we need your energy and enthusiasm to turn out the vote. For this canvass, we will be talking about the Oxford municipal elections for city commissioner and mayor.

What to Expect:

When: Saturday, August 23 at 12:30 PM

Where: GCDP Headquarters, 112 Gilliam St, Oxford

Why Canvass?

Personal Touch: Voters are more likely to turn out when someone they know (or meet!) asks them in person.

Build Community: Strengthen relationships in your neighborhood and make new friends along the way.

Impact Every Vote: Local elections hinge on small margins—your door knock could be the difference.

What to Bring:

Comfortable shoes and weather-appropriate clothing

Fully charged phone (we’ll use a simple app to track progress)

Water bottle and snack

A positive attitude and friendly smile!

We'll start at 12:30pm with a quick refresher on best practices, safety protocols, and conversation tips. Then, we'll pair-up & canvass. Grab a partner, script, and lit packet. Let’s hit the pavement together and show Oxford what grassroots power looks like. RSVP now, and we’ll see you at HQ on August 23!

We are advocating for a session to vote on passage of the IONY suite of bills, the Dignity not Detention Act, and the New York for All Act. All will help to maintain essential services, limit ICE activity in our neighborhoods, and stop ICE detention centers from being built in NY State.

We want a big turnout so that our Democratic officials can HEAR US from their offices, know that we mean business, and that we need them to step up to counteract the Trump Budget Scam and improve our living conditions! 

We will meet at West Capital Park at 10:45 am and will commence the rally promptly at 11:00 am. We have an exciting lineup of speakers including activists, community members, and elected officials. Bring a sign and come ready to MAKE SOME NOISE!
